findings.title: .gitignore blanket-ignores scripts/check_*.py, requiring a manual allowlist line per permanent gate - the likely root mechanism behind F500-008
findings.original_evidence: 3 Sep 2026, worktree gov-gates (branch feat/docs-drift-and-check-registration, base e74bd8ec): creating two new checker scripts (scripts/check_docs_drift.py, scripts/check_unregistered_checks.py) and running `git add` showed 'The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files'. `git check-ignore -v` traced both to .gitignore:196 `scripts/check_*.py`. The surrounding comment already documents one prior casualty: 'these globs are why DESIGN.md can reference a check_token_migration.py pre-commit hook that is absent from the repository - a permanent quality gate was named like a throwaway and got ignored out of existence.' Every one of the 70 check_*.py scripts currently tracked required its own `!scripts/check_X.py` negation line added by hand; the default is to silently drop a new one unless the author notices and force-adds it.
findings.required_fix: This finding was fixed rather than left open, since it was a one-line addition needed anyway to commit the two new gates: negation lines added for both new scripts. The systemic direction (default-ignore + manual allowlist for a class of file meant to be permanent) is unchanged and worth inverting - default-track scripts/check_*.py and ignore only files matching a genuinely-scratch naming convention (scripts/check_*_scratch.py, or similar) - but that broader change is out of scope of this fix and not attempted here.
findings.retest_evidence: 3 Sep 2026: both new scripts committed successfully after the negation lines were added (commit 037490fc); `git ls-files scripts/check_*.py | wc -l` -> 72 (70 pre-existing + 2 new), confirming both are now tracked.

findings.title: Firefox console diagnostics collapsed structured errors to the word Object
findings.original_evidence: Exact-SHA Firefox job in CI run 33804483255 failed the 320px motivation repository check with only `Motivation repository raised JavaScript errors: ['Object']`. Diagnostic run 33807384189 reproduced the same opaque plain-object page error at 768px, proving it arrived through Playwright's pageerror channel rather than console and still lost the thrown object's fields.
findings.required_fix: Serialize every console argument with source location, preserve page-error stacks, and install a pre-page error/unhandled-rejection probe that copies every exception into a fresh serializable diagnostic record before Firefox discards its fields.
findings.retest_evidence: Exact-SHA run 33808606132 again failed Linux Firefox with three opaque Object page errors, while its Chromium and WebKit jobs passed. Run 33810262875 then passed 55/56: the failure moved to BusinessProcess while all motivation viewports passed, and every page/API request returned 200. The first enhanced probe emitted nothing because Playwright had been given an uninvoked arrow expression; a runtime contract reproduced that absence before the probe was corrected to an IIFE. The corrected probe reproduced the failure locally on Equipment and retained the exact object: `{isFromCancelledTransition: true}`, Alpine's documented internal sentinel when one visual transition supersedes another. Archie's production error handler already prevents and ignores that exact benign signal; Playwright Firefox surfaced it before the later handler could prevent the harness pageerror. A failing-before/passing-after browser contract now makes the earliest qualification listener prevent only that exact sentinel, while an independent contract proves other plain-object rejections remain serialized and release-blocking. Seven diagnostic contracts pass locally. The complete exact 56-case Firefox compatibility command then passed 56/56 in 392.93 seconds on the corrected branch, including Equipment, BusinessProcess and all motivation viewports. Final Linux Firefox CI remains authoritative.

findings.title: CTO-tab hero Health Score and lazy-loaded Executive Summary fragment reported different values for the same metrics on the same page
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026: user-supplied screenshots of the CTO dashboard tab, same page load, taken moments apart. Hero panel: Health Score 48, Capability Coverage 100%. Executive Summary fragment (lazy-loaded via GET /dashboard/api/executive-summary): Health Score 14.3, Capability Coverage % 0. Traced: dashboard_views.py::overview computes capability coverage from ApplicationCapabilityMapping (L1 capabilities with >=1 mapped application, subtree-rolled-up); ExecutiveDashboardService._get_capability_coverage computed it from SolutionCapabilityMapping (capabilities with >=1 mapped solution - a much sparser relationship). Same label, same 20% weight in an identically-shaped 40/30/20/10 health-score composite, two different tables - an ADR-0008 violation for a computed metric rather than a stored one.
findings.proposed_fix: app/modules/dashboard/v2/services/capability_coverage.py: new compute_l1_capability_coverage(), the single shared computation (ports the hero panel exact logic). ExecutiveDashboardService._get_capability_coverage now calls it instead of reimplementing.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026, commit c2c3867a (merged to main): pytest tests/test_dashboard_capability_coverage_agreement.py -> 1 passed (seeds a capability mapped to an application but not a solution; asserts the shared function and the service call return identical dicts, not just non-conflicting numbers). pytest tests/test_dashboard_health_score_honesty.py tests/test_executive_briefing_ai.py -> 17 passed, no regression. python scripts/verify.py --tag static -> 43 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (pre-existing, unrelated). NOT fully closed: phase_maturity and risk_posture sub-components remain genuinely different formulas between the hero and the fragment (Phase-C+ percentage vs persona avg-maturity; risk severity vs risk-documentation coverage) - flagged as remaining scope, not silently left.
closure_tests: Unify phase_maturity and risk_posture the same way (not yet attempted)

findings.title: Interaction census treated wired-looking controls and rendered pages as proof that user actions worked
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026: production /solutions/32 rendered successfully and its buttons carried click-like markup, yet Link Existing Elements and Codegen produced no usable dialog. The existing tests/smoke/test_interaction_reality.py checked structural wiring and successful navigation, not the promised outcome of each visible control, allowing broken modal targets, early listener binding, recursive Alpine getters, and silent export no-ops to pass. Measured scope exposes the systemic gap: the product defines 11 enterprise roles, but the archetype journey map and interaction baseline cover only 9 (security_architect and data_architect are absent), naming only 20 unique paths; the repository contains 564 templates, 476 of them containing button/link-like controls; and the separately named Level 10 walkthrough covers only four personas and a handful of destinations.
findings.required_fix: Place the entire authenticated product in active defect scope. Inventory every reachable visible interactive control for every supported role and verify the intended navigation, modal, download, mutation, feedback, persistence, authorization, accessibility, and failure behavior in a real browser. A handler attribute, DOM presence, HTTP 200, or developer claim is not closure evidence.
findings.retest_evidence: Not yet closed. The solution detail page has been added to the interaction census and a first outcome-based Playwright journey has been added; product-wide control/outcome coverage and Linux browser execution remain outstanding.
closure_tests: Outcome-based browser journeys for every inventoried control and supported role
Complete Chromium and Firefox interaction census on the final exact release

findings.title: Solution blueprint shipped multiple visible controls whose promised outcomes did not occur
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 direct production reproduction on /solutions/32: Link Existing Elements and Codegen did not open dialogs; the phase-gate panel displayed `Error loading gate: Maximum call stack size exceeded`; Save as Template and Export OEF bound listeners before their buttons existed; modal footer Close/Done changed unused local state; PNG export silently did nothing when no renderer was available. Browser logs also reported missing modal roots and an unavailable loader-circle icon.
findings.required_fix: Give modal roots the IDs required by the modal registry, prevent phase-gate getters from recursively reading their own Alpine properties, bind header actions at interaction time, close modal-store state from footer actions, use a shipped icon, and provide visible failure feedback when PNG export is unavailable.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 strict local TDD: seven interaction-contract regressions failed against the defects and pass after repair. Template syntax, template references, and design-token gates pass. Linux CI browser run 33922010050 passed the corrected Playwright journey, which opens Deployment and clicks Link, Done, Codegen and Close while asserting modal transitions. Direct Chrome production retest on live build c913b7de then expanded Deployment and clicked Link and Codegen: both produced zero visible dialogs and no navigation, confirming production still serves the unfixed older build. Closure requires deployment of the new exact SHA followed by the same direct Chrome outcome checks.
closure_tests: Production outcome retest of every visible /solutions/<id> control

findings.title: Settings advertised fabricated backup archives and inert backup operations
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 source and rendered-contract audit: /settings hardcoded two dated ZIP archives with invented sizes and exposed Create, Download, Restore and Delete buttons despite having no backing archive service or routes. An administrator could reasonably believe recoverable backups existed when none had been created.
findings.required_fix: Remove fabricated archive records, schedules and unavailable actions. Render one explicit non-interactive unavailable state until a real repository-backed backup service exists.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026: the template now states that backup/restore are unavailable and contains no sample archives or backup controls. The PostgreSQL-backed rendered regression is pending final CI.

findings.title: Governance surfaces exposed dead shortcuts and row actions instead of canonical workflows

findings.title: Capability and plateau registers presented controls with no valid same-model workflow
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 strict TDD: the unmapped UnifiedCapability view rendered Map Application and View Details controls even though only BusinessCapability mapping/detail workflows exist, risking cross-model IDs or not-found outcomes. findings.title: Exhaustive eleven-role page auditor existed but was absent from the release workflow
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026: scripts/production_readiness_audit.py can enumerate every registered GET surface for every role at desktop and mobile widths, but no CI workflow invoked it. The release evidence instead relied on a 20-path journey map, a nine-case structural interaction census and a four-persona walkthrough while describing the result as whole-product qualification. Independent review also established that advertised L8/L10 behavior was incomplete and L6 was narrower than its documentation, so page surveying must not be represented as outcome proof.
findings.required_fix: Provide a manually dispatchable, exact-SHA CI matrix over all valid roles. Each role must run every audit level at both viewports against its own PostgreSQL 16 environment and retain its complete JSON/server-log evidence even when findings fail the job. Execute the matrix, import every finding into the active ledger, repair, and repeat until clean.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 strict TDD: the workflow contract failed because the workflow was absent, then passed after adding an eleven-role, two-viewport matrix with failure evidence retained for 30 days. The audit report inventories every visible link, button, input, select, textarea, summary and button/link role per successfully rendered page. A privacy regression then proved the first implementation captured textarea/contenteditable contents; the recorder was corrected to use associated labels and strip URL query strings. The platform-admin seed now carries real administrator permissions, expected denials are retained without failing the run, and basic admin-route allow/deny outcomes are evaluated. Six audit contract tests pass. The first exhaustive run has not yet executed, and page inventory still does not close F500-028's per-control outcome requirement.
closure_tests: Whole-product active defect audit workflow green for all 11 roles on the final SHA
All per-role JSON findings imported and dispositioned in this ledger

findings.title: Whole-product control inventory leaked editable field contents into retained CI evidence
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 independent browser reproduction against the exact PAGE_PROBE: a textarea containing 'private field contents' was serialized with that content as its label, while a normal input's associated label was missed. Contenteditable values and URL query strings could likewise enter artifacts retained for 30 days despite the recorder's no-values claim.
findings.required_fix: Resolve accessible labels without using editable text, retain no input values, and remove URL queries/fragments from recorded destinations. Enforce the guarantee in a real browser regression.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026: a Chromium regression proves input, textarea and contenteditable values are absent while aria-label and associated label text are retained. Recorded href/form actions are reduced to origin/path. Audit contract suite passes 6/6 locally.
closure_tests: Final whole-product artifacts inspected for absence of field values and URL secrets

findings.title: Whole-product matrix used a platform-admin label without administrator permissions and treated expected denials as defects
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 review of seed_personas and evaluate_findings: every seeded persona inherited the default Architect role and is_platform_admin=False, so the platform_admin matrix entry could not exercise admin pages. Every correct 401/403 was stored as an informational finding but still counted in the process exit status, making ordinary role isolation permanently fail the workflow.
findings.required_fix: Seed the platform administrator with the authoritative Administrator role and platform/org administrator flags; explicitly verify allow/deny outcomes; retain expected denial evidence without counting it as a release-blocking defect.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026: platform-admin seeding now assigns the Administrator role and admin flags. Behavioral tests distinguish expected denial, unexpected administrator denial and unauthorized non-admin access; information-only evidence is excluded from the failure count. Audit contract suite passes 6/6 locally.

findings.title: Whole-product auditor advertised journey logic without activating controls or proving outcomes
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 independent implementation review: L10 was selectable and included by default but evaluate_findings contained no L10 branch. The crawler inventoried handler attributes and successful page renders without clicking controls, reproducing the exact evidence gap behind F500-028.
findings.required_fix: For each safe visible control, start from a fresh authenticated page, activate the real control and accept only an observed navigation, popup, download, meaningful visibility/ARIA/scroll change, or successful request plus visible feedback. Block non-GET discovery traffic and explicitly defer mutation/persistence controls to seeded journeys; never credit handler presence.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 strict TDD: the L10 outcome layer records every classified control, activates safe controls on fresh pages, aborts runtime non-GET requests, emits control-no-outcome failures, sanitizes retained URLs, and incrementally flushes long-running evidence. A real Chromium test proves a handler-only button fails, a reveal succeeds, a meaningful fragment scroll succeeds and a missing fragment fails. Identical navigation destinations are deduplicated per role/viewport while page-local controls remain contextual. Focused audit suite passes 12/12 locally. The full matrix must be rerun on this implementation before closure.
closure_tests: Whole-product L10 matrix completes for all roles/viewports
Every dedicated-seeded-journey classification is mapped to a persistence/authorization/error journey

findings.title: Solution page admitted users through a bound-method bug while its visible Code Workbench action rejected them
findings.original_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 direct Chrome production test on /solutions/32, live build c913b7de: More actions opened, but clicking its visible Code Workbench menu item navigated to a 403 Forbidden page. Source trace found _check_solution_access used `if user.is_admin`, which treats the bound method itself as truthy and admits every authenticated same-tenant user, while codegen _check_access correctly called the method but recognized only creator/admin and omitted named stakeholders and the is_platform_admin flag. Smoke fixtures concealed this disagreement by assigning the Administrator role to all 11 personas.
findings.required_fix: Invoke is_admin rather than testing the method object, recognize the explicit platform-admin flag, and make blueprint and Code Workbench access agree for creators, administrators and named stakeholders. Give ordinary smoke personas Architect permissions and only the platform_admin persona Administrator permissions. Prove the visible menu destination in a real browser using a platform administrator who did not create the solution.
findings.retest_evidence: 4 Sep 2026 strict TDD: focused tests failed because an outsider was admitted by the bound method and codegen accepted no explicit user. Both access checks now agree for denial, creator, named stakeholder and platform administrator; 9/9 access plus blueprint interaction contracts pass locally. A new Playwright journey clicks More actions then Code Workbench as a non-creator platform administrator and requires the real workbench heading rather than a 403. Linux CI, deployment and direct production Chrome retest remain required.
closure_tests: Direct production Chrome click from More actions to a rendered Code Workbench

findings.title: Click auditor marked navigation to HTTP error pages as verified
findings.original_evidence: Chromium regression against a local HTTP server proved that clicks to 403, 404 and 500 pages were all classified as verified navigation by the new L10 probe. Only the URL change was checked. This would conceal the same workbench failure observed directly in production.
findings.required_fix: Require a captured main-frame destination response and reject HTTP errors before accepting navigation evidence. Exercise successful and failed destinations in Chromium.
findings.retest_evidence: The regression first failed for all three error statuses while the 200 case passed. After the correction all four navigation cases and the complete focused audit suite passed, 16 tests total. CI and application-level outcome qualification remain outstanding.

Real route tests confirmed all three handlers admitted non-administrators: index returned 200, upgrade reached organization validation and portal redirected, instead of rejecting access before billing operations.

findings.title: Browser audit falsely reported named account switches as unnamed
findings.original_evidence: The account template labels each notification switch using aria-labelledby. PAGE_PROBE ignored those references when inspecting buttons, yielding twenty false unnamed-button observations per completed role across two account routes and viewports.
findings.required_fix: Resolve aria-labelledby text when testing button names and continue reporting missing or empty references.
findings.retest_evidence: Chromium regression confirms a correctly referenced switch is accepted while a missing label reference remains a finding. Combined billing and audit suite passes 15 tests. Original observations remain retained for traceability.

findings.title: Deprecation monitoring dashboard and APIs admitted ordinary users in both implementations
findings.original_evidence: The first browser surveys flagged /admin/deprecation/ for ordinary architect accounts. Actual route tests reproduced 200 responses in both legacy and v2 implementations. Five monitoring GET routes lacked administrator checks; the legacy alert-sending POST also lacked an administrator guard.
findings.required_fix: Require existing administrator permission before rendering monitoring pages, reading metrics or invoking alert delivery in both implementations.
findings.retest_evidence: Both dashboard denial regressions failed before repair. After repair, 16 deprecation tests pass, including Chromium clicks through the real registered routes for ordinary/admin accounts in both implementations, plus API tests proving denied requests do not call metrics services. Combined billing/deprecation suite passes 24 tests. Rendered data is stubbed in these isolated permission tests; full application CI and production verification remain outstanding.
closure_tests: Full application role matrix and production administration access retest

findings.title: Five rationalization and workflow pages render duplicate breadcrumb trails
findings.original_evidence: Browser survey 33923515022 recorded duplicate-breadcrumbs on rationalization enrich, tracking, workbench, workflow definitions and phase viewpoint pages in both desktop and mobile. Source confirms each template renders an explicit contextual trail plus a second trail through page_shell or page_header.
findings.required_fix: Render only the contextual trail and verify the visible parent link navigates successfully in the application browser.
findings.retest_evidence: Removed redundant breadcrumb arguments from the five header calls, preserving contextual parent navigation. Template syntax gate passes. Added five full-application Playwright cases requiring one visible breadcrumb and successful parent navigation; those browser cases still require CI execution. No browser-verified closure is claimed.
closure_tests: Production visual and breadcrumb navigation checks
